scope.quote: DIVISION 26 – ELECTRICAL – REFER TO ELECTRICAL DRAWINGS
scope.statement: Division 26 and 27 technical requirements must be obtained from the referenced electrical and telecommunications drawings; this manual contains no dedicated sections for those divisions. Division 28 is listed not used, which does not resolve drawing-based fire-alarm or security work.

scope.quote: Runs of vertical and horizontal conduit 1-1/4 inches in diameter and larger.
scope.statement: Prepare interdisciplinary coordination drawings showing electrical device/equipment locations, conduit 1-1/4 inches and larger, and dimensioned pull/junction boxes. Coordinate plenum space, access and structural penetrations.

scope.quote: Perform three-dimensional component conflict analysis as part of preparation of coordination drawings.
scope.statement: Carry BIM coordination and three-dimensional conflict analysis; resolve conflicts before submission.

scope.quote: Before proceeding with installing work that will conceal other work, take photographs sufficient in number, with annotated descriptions, to record nature and location of concealed Work
scope.statement: Photograph electrical conduit and other concealed electrical services with annotated descriptions before concealment; coordinate this with general contractor documentation.

scope.quote: Provide connections and extensions of services as required for construction operations.
scope.statement: Provide construction power connections/extensions from Owner's existing system, subject to UMC procedures for metering and use; allocation between general contractor and electrical subcontractor is not specified.

scope.quote: Provide electrical power service and 120V ac duplex receptacles, with no fewer than one receptacle on each wall.
scope.statement: Temporary common-use office needs 120V ac duplex receptacles at least one per wall, electrical power service, lighting averaging 20 foot-candles at desk height and conditioned space. Wall count, HVAC load and service capacity are not stated.

scope.quote: Provide single switch for emergency shut off. Configure to run continuously.
scope.statement: Coordinate continuous power for temporary HEPA negative-air equipment and its single emergency shutoff switch. No unit count, voltage or amperage is provided.

scope.quote: Install and operate temporary lighting that fulfills security and protection requirements without operating entire system.
scope.statement: Provide locally switched temporary construction/security lighting and maintain temporary electrical equipment in Owner-acceptable condition.

scope.quote: Provide secure WiFi wireless connection to internet with provisions for access by Architect and Owner.
scope.statement: Secure construction WiFi for Architect and Owner is required; confirm whether furnished by general contractor or low-voltage subcontractor.

scope.quote: Barricades, Warning Signs, and Lights: Comply with requirements of authorities having jurisdiction
scope.statement: Maintain access/egress and barricade warning lights as required; protect existing utilities. Coordinate elevator, stair, parking and staging permissions with UMC.

scope.quote: Do not change over from using temporary security and protection facilities to permanent facilities until Substantial Completion.
scope.statement: Maintain required temporary environmental facilities continuously and remove temporary electrical facilities when authorized, restoring affected permanent work.

scope.quote: including materials and equipment furnished by the Owner for the Contractor to install
scope.statement: Protect owner-furnished equipment to be installed and equipment furnished/installed by Owner's separate contractors within the work; this is not evidence that any particular electrical equipment is owner-furnished.

scope.quote: Providing routine penetrations of non-structural surfaces for installation of piping electrical conduit, and similar items.
scope.statement: Include routine conduit penetrations and coordinated cutting/patching; obtain consent for cuts affecting other trades, structures, waterproofing, operations or finished appearance.

scope.quote: Fit Work airtight to pipes, sleeves, ducts, conduit and other penetrations through surfaces.
scope.statement: Seal penetrations airtight and preserve fire ratings; restoration may extend to whole finish surfaces or nearest corner/intersection. Coordinate original installers for exposed/weatherproof finish repairs.

scope.quote: Complete startup and testing of systems and equipment.
scope.statement: Complete electrical startup/testing, preventive maintenance for equipment used before completion, required AHJ releases, records, O&M, spare-material delivery, owner training and demonstration recordings before closeout.

scope.quote: Clean luminaires, lamps, globes, and reflectors to function with full efficiency.
scope.statement: Clean electrical equipment and all luminaire optical surfaces for final turnover.

scope.quote: Revisions to electrical circuitry.
scope.statement: Maintain actual electrical routing/circuitry and concealed-condition record drawings, including underground depths/locations; record before concealment.

scope.quote: Conduct selective demolition so Owner's operations will not be disrupted.
scope.statement: Owner occupies immediately adjacent areas throughout demolition; protect ongoing operations and verify disconnections before starting. Owner handles hazardous-material removal under separate contract.

scope.quote: Provide connections, supports, and miscellaneous materials necessary to make item functional for use indicated.
scope.statement: For relocated/reinstalled electrical items identified elsewhere, provide cleaning/repair, secure storage, new connections and supports necessary for functional reuse. Confirm salvage inventory with Owner.

scope.quote: Equipment Backing Panels: Plywood, DOC PS 1, Exterior, A-C
scope.statement: Coordinate electrical/telecom equipment backing with carpentry; minimum plywood thickness 5/8 inch nominal where not otherwise indicated, with fire-retardant treatment required by following page.

scope.quote: Shop-cut openings to maximum extent possible to receive hardware, appliances, plumbing fixtures, electrical work, and similar items.
scope.statement: Supply electrical rough-in diagrams/templates to cabinet fabricator before shop cutouts; coordinate receptacles and data routing with cable-management accessories.

scope.quote: Do not cover up firestop system installations that will become concealed behind other construction until each installation has been examined by Owner's inspecting agency and building inspector
scope.statement: Coordinate rated electrical penetrations with tested firestop systems, qualified installer and inspections before concealment. Trade assignment is not expressly divided.

scope.quote: Attach labels permanently to surfaces adjacent to and within 6 inches of edge of the firestop systems
scope.statement: Provide permanent identification labels at firestop systems and repair failed installations before concealment.

scope.quote: Coordinate locations of conduit and wiring boxes for electrical connections with Division 26 Sections.
scope.statement: Coordinate electrical conduit and box locations with hollow-metal door/frame manufacturer and electrified hardware provider.

scope.quote: Provide built-in 1/4 inch diameter raceway through doors, from lockset location to nearest hinge location, for low voltage wiring for doors scheduled to have electric locks.
scope.statement: Wood door fabricator must provide internal wiring raceway for doors scheduled for electric locks; field wiring and connections require coordination with hardware sets.

scope.quote: Door Locks (Optional):
scope.statement: AD Systems magnetic lock appears as an optional sliding-door component. Confirm selection and furnishing/installation split before including power supply, raceways, controls and release interfaces; electrical ratings are absent.

summary: This group contains the 166-page architectural project manual, a two-page Uniweb prewired-panel brochure, and a two-page UMC door hardware standard. The manual does not contain Division 26 or 27 specifications; it directs the reader to electrical and telecommunications drawings and lists Division 28 as not used. Electrical bid requirements include temporary power and lighting, occupied-facility protection, coordination drawings and BIM conflict analysis, submittals, concealed-work documentation, testing/startup, record documents, O&M manuals, and owner training. Architectural sections add electrical penetration firestopping, acoustical seals and box putty pads, equipment backing, casework coordination, and electrified-door interfaces. Uniweb configurations are explicitly samples, not project quantities or selected assemblies. Door hardware requirements identify owner-standard electronic locks, automatic operators, electrified closers, and delayed-egress locks, but do not establish opening quantities or electrical connection data. The roller-shade specification conflicts between manual operation and an instruction to connect motor-operated shades, requiring clarification.
